evidence.claim: The Indian Heritage Trail belongs to North Carolina’s scenic-byway collection.
evidence.quote: Indian Heritage Trail 150

evidence.claim: The North Carolina Department of Transportation selects these roads to introduce the state’s history, geography and culture.
evidence.quote: The N.C. Department of Transportation has designated 62 scenic byways to give visitors and residents a chance to experience North Carolina’s history, geography, and culture

evidence.claim: In this part of the Piedmont, Mount Gilead sits on a ridge draining toward tributaries of the Pee Dee River.
evidence.quote: The town sits on a ridge that drains northwest toward Clarks Creek, a tributary of the Pee Dee River, and southeast toward Hamer Creek, a tributary of the Little River, also part of the Pee Dee watershed.

evidence.claim: At Town Creek, professional archaeological work began in 1937 with Works Progress Administration funding.
evidence.quote: In 1937 professional archaeologists began a Works Progress Administration (WPA)-funded project during the Great Depression.

evidence.claim: The state later reconstructed a ceremonial center, restoring the mound and rebuilding a temple on it.
evidence.quote: It built a reconstructed ceremonial center, restoring the platform mound and reconstructing a temple on it.

evidence.claim: Before this Richmond County town was Ellerbe, it was the Fair Grounds: Scottish settlers held fairs here each May and November in the 1700s.
evidence.quote: In the 1700s Scottish settlers held a fair every May and November in the present location of Ellerbe, leading locals to dub the place "the Fair Grounds".

evidence.claim: The name changed after W. T. Ellerbe developed the nearby Ellerbe Springs spa.
evidence.quote: W. T. Ellerbe later developed a spa nearby called Ellerbe Springs, and thereafter the community took its name.

evidence.claim: A railroad and depot arrived in 1910, followed by incorporation in 1911, when the population was just 50.
evidence.quote: A railroad was built to Ellerbe in 1910 and a depot was constructed. The town was incorporated the following year. At the time it only had a population of 50.

evidence.claim: By 1923, the population had grown to more than 500. Several mills operated alongside two banks, three churches, a telephone exchange and a hotel.
evidence.quote: By 1923 it had grown to a population of over 500, with several mills, two banks, three churches, a telephone exchange, and a hotel.

evidence.claim: Rail service ended in 1954; the depot burned several years later.
evidence.quote: The rail line remained in service until 1954, and the depot burnt down several years later.

evidence.claim: The Pee Dee built their mound on a low bluff where Town Creek meets the Little River.
evidence.quote: The Pee Dee people built their mound on a low bluff at the confluence of Town Creek and the Little River.

evidence.claim: The earthwork covered the remains of a rectangular earth lodge.
evidence.quote: The earthwork mound was built over the remains of a rectangular-shaped earth lodge.

evidence.claim: Archaeologists found a sequence of buildings: a collapsed lodge, a temple above it that burned, and another ceremonial structure on the mound.
evidence.quote: The earliest structure was a rectangular earth lodge that had collapsed with age. The second structure was built over the fallen lodge; it was a temple. After the temple burned, the Pee Dee built another ceremonial structure on the same spot on top of the mound.

evidence.claim: The structures presented by the state are reconstructions, including a temple on the restored mound and a mortuary.
evidence.quote: It built a reconstructed ceremonial center, restoring the platform mound and reconstructing a temple on it. It also reconstructed a minor temple and the mortuary.

evidence.claim: The Pee Dee people are based in South Carolina today.
evidence.quote: Today the Pee Dee people are based in South Carolina

evidence.claim: The temple on the restored platform mound is a reconstruction.
evidence.quote: restoring the platform mound and reconstructing a temple on it.

evidence.claim: Mount Gilead incorporated in 1899 as textile mills spread through the Piedmont.
evidence.quote: Mount Gilead was incorporated in 1899 as the textile industry built mills in the Piedmont region of the state

evidence.claim: The mills processed cotton and employed white residents before later employing Black residents as well.
evidence.quote: They processed the commodity crop of cotton, which had been important to the South since before the Civil War. The textile mills provided jobs to white residents of the region, later also employing blacks

evidence.claim: When textile work moved offshore in the late twentieth century, the town lost jobs and population.
evidence.quote: Since the late 20th century, many textile jobs moved offshore in a restructuring of the industry as it sought lower labor costs. Like many small southern towns, Mount Gilead suffered economic and population decline following the loss of these textile jobs.

evidence.claim: Its downtown historic district entered the National Register in 2005.
evidence.quote: The Mount Gilead Downtown Historic District has been inventoried and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2005.

evidence.claim: Near downtown, the Mount Gilead Museum occupies the McAulay family’s restored Victorian house, with documents, photographs and artifacts tracing the town’s past.
evidence.quote: The Mount Gilead Museum is located in a restored Victorian house near the downtown area. The house belonged to the McAulay family, who played an important role in Mount Gilead business, church, social, and civic life.  The museum houses many documents, photographs, and historic artifacts that tell the story of Mount Gilead's past.

evidence.claim: The state’s visitor center interprets the site through exhibits and audiovisual programs, while trails extend across the property.
evidence.quote: The visitor center houses interpretive exhibits, audiovisual programs, and a gift shop.

evidence.claim: trails extend across the property.
evidence.quote: Several trails and outdoor monuments are located on the property.

evidence.claim: In this part of the Piedmont
evidence.quote: Mount Gilead is a town in Montgomery County, in the Piedmont region of North Carolina

evidence.claim: Landowner L. D. Frutchey donated the mound and about an acre of surrounding land to North Carolina.
evidence.quote: Frutchey donated the mound and about an acre of surrounding land to the state of North Carolina

evidence.claim: In Mount Gilead, NC 73 is Main Street.
evidence.quote: North Carolina Highway 73 passes through the center of town as Main Street

evidence.claim: Town Creek Indian Mound lies five miles southeast of town.
evidence.quote: is 5 miles (8 km) southeast of Mount Gilead.

evidence.claim: NC 73 leads southeast from Mount Gilead to Ellerbe.
evidence.quote: North Carolina Highway 73 passes through the center of town as Main Street, leading northwest 16 miles (26 km) to Albemarle and southeast 18 miles (29 km) to Ellerbe.

evidence.claim: this Richmond County town
evidence.quote: Ellerbe is a town in Richmond County, North Carolina

evidence.claim: The town also received a $220,000 S.T.E.P. grant intended to help revitalize downtown and create jobs.
evidence.quote: received a S.T.E.P. (Small Town Economic Prosperity) grant of $220,000 to help revitalize the downtown area and create jobs, respectively.
